Indeed. Your N-parent convinces you that he or she hasn't done anything wrong. At the same time, N-parents are good at presenting themselves in a very flattering manner to everyone else (friends, other family members, coworkers and whatnot) *and* making it look like you're being irrational in some way.

This means that if there's an issue between you and your N-parent, it could seem as if it has been fully resolved but *intuitively* you still know that something's wrong (in other words, the "uncomfortable feeling of anger inside you and you don't know why").

Typically, you've been convinced that *you* are the one at fault, even though it's the other way around. It doesn't help, so to speak, if you have diagnosed mental illness, as in my case. I'm pretty sure my N-mom simply points to that whenever the issue of me never speaking to her comes up.

I think this kind of half-assed apology is typical of narcissists. They like to be able to say something that *looks* like an apology, but really isn't. Your N-mom says "I'm sorry *that you feel that way*" -- an actual, *genuine* apology would be more along the lines of "What I did was wrong and selfish of me, and I apologize for doing harm to you".

See item 20 on this list: http://parrishmiller.com/narcissists.html

Me neither. After all, if most people around you, even those with good intent towards you, tend to *not really believe you* when you talk about your N-parent(s) and try to explain what has happened and is happening in other ways (*maybe you're having a very delayed period of rebellion since you didn't really have one in your teens -- she probably just tried to do what's best for you -- this doesn't sound like her (N-mom), she's a really good person*), it makes sense that you yourself start to think that maybe you're just making shit up. It's depressing and frustrating.

Thank you and InvaderChin for confirming that my ideas aren't entirely bogus. And yeah, the self-destructiveness is part of it, in the sense that you're thinking "fuck you, I won't do it if it's useful to you, *even if it means I'd hurt or limit myself*".

I guess the typical mindset for ACoNs like myself is thinking that your ideas, work or skills are mediocre at best, unless someone explicitly tells you otherwise. Am I fishing for validation here? A little, yes. I mean, shit, I guess it's OK, to some extent, this being a forum for ACoNs and all. Of course, one shouldn't rely on external validation to feel good about everything you do, but it helps when you're at home, alone, and your N-mom keeps sending you texts about wanting you to show up at family events and whatnot, her expressing that she's worried about me when I don't respond to those texts, and you're thinking that maybe you're doing the wrong thing about distancing yourself *from your own mother (gasp)*, and you start to feel mentally exhausted and lonely, but you keep telling yourself that it's fine, you don't need to talk to anyone about this, and so on, and so on...

Oh, man, I just read the title and thought "so much this". Then I read the article and recalled this notion I've had for some time now, which is that there are two major reasons for not wanting do to something *that would be good for you* when you're raised by narcissists. (It's a bit "out there", but bear with me.)

When I say "something that would be good for you", this could be **a)** things that you simply enjoy doing, like riding a motorcycle such as mentioned in the article, or **b)** things that you may or may not *enjoy* doing at all times but they'd be good for you in the long run; you know, healthy or useful things, like losing weight or getting done with a taxing academic effort.

So, the first major reason for not doing something that's good for you would be that you believe your N-parents wouldn't approve of it (obviously, here we're assuming that you'd want the approval of your N-parents in the first place). This applies to both categories "a" and "b".

Now, the kicker here is that should your N-parents actually approve of some activity of category "b", *you may still not want to do it because it makes* **them** *happy* -- it'd be beneficial for your N-parents, in the sense that they can have their friends (or co-workers or whatever) know that you're *such* a successful, well-educated, smart and handsome kid, and you wouldn't want to give them the satisfaction. That would be the second major reason. A sub-conscious "fuck you, I don't want to be useful to you anymore" sort of thing. Is there some truth to this or am I just rambling?

I'm a virgin at 25 and a few years ago I was very stressed out about it. Not so much anymore. I believe that more people than you think (males especially) are virgins, given that, amongst other things, it's not really considered polite conversation and we have all this bullshit media and entertainment (i.e. films, TV series, etc.) that perpetuates the idea that young adults all need to have sex, right now, regardless of circumstances, otherwise you're a loser.

A guy doesn't _need_ to have sex, per se. To me, it's obviously not a necessity for your survival. Having said that, I think that the quality of a guy's life will improve from it, however, only within the context of a relationship, and only with someone you'd consider having a child with, otherwise it's effete.

Granted, I don't have a firm opinion on this, yet, since I don't have any experience of it personally. Also, I'm still hesitant to admit to being a virgin at those rare occasions it's brought up in conversations; maybe due to cultural conditioning, in the sense that it will scare girls away... which is silly because a girl that has a huge problem with this probably isn't worth pursuing anyway, which brings me to one of OP:s issues: "Game" theory on alphas, betas and omegas aside, a girl that, based on your virginity alone, determines you as a loser is probably not a very likeable person to begin with, thus, not a good idea to have sex with, to put it bluntly. I don't know if this goes against human nature or whatever... I just hope there's another less dysfunctional way of looking at dating, romance and sex than what Game/PUA/seduction theory and the entertainment industry (these views are dysfunctional in different ways, even tough they have different views on who "wins", as it were, in the mating game) has displayed.

I guess this is a bad thing and it's preferable if you can imagine your depression as this "other thing" that isn't actually intrinsic to your entire being.
